guitar.evidence: Chris Britton of The Troggs played typical mid-60s British Invasion-era electrics, but no singularly iconic documented instrument for 'Wild Thing'.

tone.target: raw garage fuzz crunch with dirty mono bite
tone.profile: raw garage fuzz crunch with dirty mono bite
tone.summary: A raw, fuzzy signal chain using a Fuzz distortion unit into an AC30-style amp, paired with a vintage cabinet to capture the dirty, nasal sound of 60s garage rock.
corrections: make it grittier and less bluesy

rig.name: The Troggs - Wild Thing - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise inherent in raw fuzz tones.
Provide the core fuzzy attack and raw grit required for garage rock.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative if Fuzz is too aggressive, offering more control.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the mids to ensure the 'nasal' bite cuts through the fuzz.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is general; a dedicated EQ might be better, but this keeps the chain simple and focused on raw tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British combo amp sound (like a small 60s/70s rig) that handles fuzz well without sounding overly polished.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a smaller, punchier British sound.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet tone that complements the AC30 and adds necessary grit.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more aggressive, dirty alternative.

blocks.purpose: Fine-tune the mids to achieve the required 'bright nasal' bite and cut through the fuzz.
Optional subtle modulation for texture, but kept off to maintain raw simplicity.
blocks.gap: The genre doesn't require modulation, so this is a placeholder/optional effect. It can be bypassed entirely.

blocks.purpose: Kept off to maintain the raw, immediate feel of garage rock.
blocks.gap: None. Delay is generally unnecessary for this style.

improvements.summary: Replace the cabinet IR with a dirtier, more aggressive 60s/70s style speaker to enhance the raw garage fuzz bite.

proposals.reason: Needs a dirtier, more aggressive 60s/70s speaker sound to match the raw garage fuzz.
